significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) behavioral law: for several conceptual mappings, accuracy follows “CONGRUENT > NEUTRAL > INCONGRUENT,” errors preferentially follow the metaphor-default direction, and a metaphor-neutral restatement reverses much of the loss. This fixes predictions for further logically equivalent reframings and establishes a substantial phenomenon, but the proposed “covert reasoning scaffolds” remain a behavioral causal account rather than a specific internal mechanism; human findings such as Boroditsky’s space-time congruency studies and Casasanto’s spatial-valence work show why this pattern bears directly on theories of language-mediated cognition. Verified false would meaningfully rule out this scaffold account for the tested metaphor classes and models, although it would not establish metaphor-independent reasoning generally; the two branches are therefore distinguishable and informative. The topic-substitution check lowers no credit here: “language affects AI intelligence” alone would not earn this score, whereas the predicted ordering, directional-error coupling, and neutralization effect are specific constraints beyond the median framing-effect hypothesis.

reach.justification: The claim supplies two named handles: the “per-model congruency effect (congruent minus incongruent accuracy)” as an auditing quantity and the instruction to “first restate the problem in metaphor-neutral, purely relational terms” as an intervention. The latter is ex ante because it can be applied before solving or deployment, while the asserted congruent-neutral-incongruent ordering and directional-error signature predict what should recur after measurement is recalibrated on another model rather than merely providing a procedure for searching. Scope spans four metaphor classes, multiple task types, model families, and sizes, though it is explicitly anchored to English-dominant mappings; downstream users include benchmark designers and practitioners auditing prompts for robustness, not only metaphor researchers. The topic-substitution check passes because the broad language–intelligence topic offers neither this metric nor the pre-solution neutralization rule, so the reach comes from the claim-specific transferable relation and action window.
